state:
**Goal `ldap` — Stage 2 is done: ADR 0278 and its six fragments are on disk, and nothing of the wire or the class has landed.** `docs/decisions/0278.md` is the design every later stage builds to: § 1 is the class and member roster, § 2 the `[ldap.<name>]` block, `Ldap\Settings` and the three `[capabilities.ldap]` grants (`connect`, `open`, `cleartext`), § 5 search, § 8 the type table, § 10 the error kinds, § 11 the four AD extras (`uSNChanged` polling is left out; DirSync is the one sync form, as `Connection::changes`). Read the section a stage needs rather than the whole record.

The six fragments are `designed` with empty `guardedBy`: `core-classes/ldap-filter-is-a-value`, `ldap-dn-is-the-launderer`, `ldap-value-types`, `security/ldap-empty-password-is-refused`, `ldap-cleartext-bind-is-granted-per-host`, `ldap-pool-is-bound-as-its-block`. A stage that lands the guard adds the test path to the rule's JSON under `data/rules/` and flips `status` to `shipped`.

Stage 10 of `data/goals/ldap.json` now carries one `proofs --verify --group` check per member-bearing class the record names (12), and the `--comments` check lists every class's `Ldap-*` directory. If a later stage renames a class, those checks move with it.

`bun nv rules --check` is clean: the `pdf` and `spreadsheet` goal files now name the rules they will create without the `rule:` prefix, as this goal's prose does.

next.note: first file set: the test server (`tests/db/compose.yaml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `tools/nv/cmd/db-matrix.ts`, `data/goals/ldap.json`).

items.text: **The `samba-ad` service** — `smblds/smblds` pinned by digest, a fixed `hostname`, loopback ports 16389 and 16636, a health check, no `--privileged`, `ldap server require strong auth = no` so the cleartext path is testable; its name joins the `certs` leaf's SAN at `tests/db/compose.yaml:90`, and the service sits beside `tests/db/compose.yaml:294` (`redis`). `rule:security/ldap-cleartext-bind-is-granted-per-host`.

**`env.docker` naming `samba-ad` in `data/goals/ldap.json`**, in the same slice as the service, and an `ldap` step in CI beside the Redis one at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:275`; `tools/nv/cmd/db-matrix.ts:343` (`bringUp`) is where the matrix brings services up.

**`crates/nvs-ldap`** (second file set: the new crate, `Cargo.toml`, `deny.toml`) — a sans-IO codec checked for no tokio (`crates/nvs-runtime/tests/manifest_policy.rs:148`), bind, StartTLS over `crates/nvs-host/src/tls.rs:224`, unbind, paged search, the empty-password refusal, result codes as kinds. `rule:core-classes/db-crate-boundary`, ADR 0278 § 3 and § 5.

backlog: Stages 4 to 9: `Core\Ldap` connect/open/search, the filter builder and `Dn`, typed values, writes and passwords, `authenticate`, the AD extras — under `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/`, to ADR 0278 § 1–§ 11.
Stage 10: the feature proofs, one `Ldap-*` directory per class (`docs/agent/goals/ldap.md`).
Stage 0's closing search, `grep -rn -i ldap docs/rules docs/reference crates`, is owed now the record exists (`docs/agent/goals/ldap.md` § Stage 0).
A run against a Windows Server evaluation VM is the user's to do by hand; a gap it finds comes back here.
